done_when: The generated forge.yml that gates merging runs the tests as the parallel groups, with one required check that passes only when every group passes, for this repo and for client repos on init and after upgrade and sync

findings.body: Raise: Functional. For any repo whose generated workflow has six groups, `ships()` appends split flags to `cfg["test"]` before writing the `run:` line. The unchanged `forge doctor` check at `src/forge/doctor.py:409-410` looks for the original command as an exact `run:` line, so it reports that the tests check does not run the configured command and exits with an error even immediately after a successful sync. This affects Forge's own repo and split-enabled clients.
findings.title: forge doctor rejects healthy split workflows

findings.body: Raise: Test. The proof list names `test_1` for new clients, but its init assertion checks only a one-group workflow. It adds a pytest-split pyproject and checks six groups only after `forge sync` (lines 43-46 and 70-81). A regression where `forge init` fails to generate six groups for a new client that already lists pytest-split would leave this proof green, so the Done-when init behavior lacks its command-level test.
findings.title: Not done: test six split groups at new-client init

stop.reason: Coordinator decision (Harm 2, nothing dropped): one more round; the latest commit fixes both open findings, so the review checks it

why: The check that gates merging runs the whole suite as one 35-minute job; the six faster test groups run only in a workflow nothing waits on
